stories.title: Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule
stories.body: Women across the country speak of public floggings, losing their jobs, and barriers to healthcare that endanger lives.

stories.title: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
stories.body: BBC's Top Comment podcast has found a network of Instagram profiles glamourising the swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence.

stories.title: Activists try to deliver aid to Palestinians in homes besieged by Israeli settlers
stories.body: Two families have been trapped in their homes in the occupied West Bank for several days.

stories.title: 'Unprecedented' rain in Japan kills eight people
stories.body: The storm cut power to more than 20,000 households and left 7,000 people stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport.

stories.title: Builders unearth €9m gold stash sealed in walls of Belgian property
stories.body: Construction workers found the stash in the walls of a cellar while drilling to lay sewage pipes.

stories.title: Stolen Matisse artworks recovered by police in Brazil
stories.body: A man is arrested after eight works by the French artist are found at a home in greater São Paulo.

stories.title: Dozens injured and thousands evacuated in Croatia wildfire
stories.body: Officials say the blaze, near the port town of Omis, is one of the worst in Croatia's history.

stories.title: France's top court blocks social media ban for under-15s
stories.body: The Constitutional Council says it infringes upon freedom of expression - but President Macron vows to prepare a new draft.

stories.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to allow ballroom work to continue
stories.body: Forcing the US president to go "hat-in-hand to Congress" for permission would be "dangerous", the administration says.

stories.title: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
stories.body: The electoral commission said violence had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers".

stories.title: UK diplomats no longer get hardship bonus for being posted to Buenos Aires
stories.body: Civil servants are entitled to extra money for working in difficult or dangerous cities around the world.

stories.title: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms
stories.body: Thousands of sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

stories.title: US says dozens of countries helped China dodge Trump's tariffs
stories.body: A new US report said China had moved goods through nations with lower tariffs to dodge higher levies.

stories.title: Engine parts smashed Ryanair window that man's head was sucked out of, report says
stories.body: A preliminary report by US investigators says an engine fan blade broke on last month's flight from Greece to Germany.

stories.title: US missionary released following kidnap in Niger, Christian group says
stories.body: Kevin Rideout, who was kidnapped outside his home in the capital last October, is now with US officials.

stories.title: Palestinians told to leave homes in village where Israeli settlers besieged houses
stories.body: The mayor of Qusra says Israeli troops have been telling families to leave their houses, using some as barracks.

stories.title: Person fined after using foghorn to wake sleeping polar bear
stories.body: Under local regulations in the region, "it is forbidden to needlessly disturb, attract or pursue a polar bear".

stories.title: Romania shuts only nuclear plant as heat causes huge drop in Danube River level
stories.body: The Cernavodă plant, which produces 20% of Romania's electricity, is not expected to be restarted within the next 10 days.

stories.title: Air India to test all pilots for banned substances
stories.body: It comes after one of its planes suddenly lost altitude last week, with a number of passengers injured.

stories.title: Teens who fled Venezuela after deadly quakes caught in another disaster in Colombia
stories.body: Deivi Delfín and his brother moved to Colombia after a quake in Venezuela killed their mother, but were caught in another deadly disaster.
